validity.recommendation: Keep as-is; attach the three refs below for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Owner/Location/Start. This is one of the better-corroborated rows in the scope - real, named, SSGC-owned transmission line with a specific field-to-city purpose. See the two companion 'spec' entries for open caveats on Length and Capacity.
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki 403'd this run (wiki_citations.json empty), so this was ground-up open-web research, not re-verification of an existing citation. EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, and NOT GEM-derived. Three independent, non-GEM sources all name this exact line: (1) SSGC's own website (Urdu newsroom), 'SSGC's Team Conducts GPS Survey of Zarghun-Quetta Pipeline' (ssgc.com.pk/urdu/?p=558), describing an in-house GPS/satellite re-route survey of the 'Zarghun-Quetta Pipeline' carried out by SSGC's IT department in May 2013, following earlier private-contractor surveys in 2004 and 2009, and noting SSGC decided in 2006 to build the line but was delayed by law-and-order issues in Balochistan before resuming construction in 2012; (2) a peer-reviewed paper in the Journal of Basic & Applied Sciences, 'Demarcation of Right of Way (ROW) and Re-Installation of Damaged Markers of Transmission Pipeline in Balochistan, Pakistan... A Case Study of Zarghun to Quetta High Pressure Natural Gas Supply' (setpublisher.com/index.php/jbas/article/view/1274), an academic, independently-editorially-reviewed source that repeats and corroborates the same construction/survey history and explicitly calls it a 'gas transmission pipeline from Zarghun gas fields to Quetta city' operated by SSGC; (3) The Balochistan Post (2024-06), reporting an armed attack on the 'Zarghun gas field' installation near Quetta, confirming the field/pipeline complex is still an active, physically real, guarded piece of infrastructure as of mid-2024, not a paper project. A fourth source, a Rigzone-hosted Jura Energy Corp press release dated 2014-11-14 ('Pakistan's Zarghun South Field Surface Processing Facilities Operational', reached via Wayback Machine archive since the live Rigzone URL redirect-loops for the verifier), independently confirms the upstream Zarghun South field - operated by Mari Petroleum Company Limited, 40% working interest held by Jura Energy - completed full commissioning of its surface processing facilities in November 2014 and began supplying sales gas that 'meets the specification requirements provided under the Gas Sale and Purchase Agreement with SSGCL [Sui Southern Gas Company Limited]', i.e. SSGC. This independently corroborates GEM's StartYear1=2014 (commissioning press release dated Nov 2014) and confirms the SSGC offtake relationship that this pipeline physically represents. CLASSIFICATION: correct. Both the SSGC source and the academic paper explicitly and repeatedly describe this as a 'transmission pipeline' / 'High Pressure Natural Gas Supply' line, not a gathering or distribution line - PipelineType=transmission is right, and Fuel=Gas is trivially correct (all sources describe natural gas). ATTRIBUTION: Owner = Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% is confirmed by SSGC's own site (it is literally SSGC's own project/survey) and by the academic paper, which names SSGC as the owner/executor of the pipeline construction and survey work. LOCATION: Start=Zarghun/Balochistan, End=Quetta/Balochistan is confirmed by every source - the SSGC source specifically names the route as running from 'Zarghun South-1' to 'Quetta TBS' (town border station), and the academic paper's title is literally 'Zarghun to Quetta'. DUPLICATE check against the 63-row roster: no conflict. P4021 'Quetta Gas Pipeline' (Jacobabad->Balochistan) is a different, longer (344 km) trunk line bringing Sui-system gas into Quetta from the north/Sindh direction; P4022 is the short, distinct local feeder from the Zarghun South field itself (57 km NE of Quetta in Harnai District) into the city. These are two separate, non-overlapping physical assets serving the same city from different directions/sources - not a relabel or segment double-count.

validity.recommendation: Leave Length as-is (61 km) but note the ~5% gap; not material enough to force a change, but flag for a future pass with a more precise SSGC as-built schedule.
validity.researcher_notes: SSGC's own Urdu-language survey article (ssgc.com.pk/urdu/?p=558) states the pipeline runs 'approximately 64 kilometers from Zarghun South-1 to Quetta TBS' - GEM's LengthKnown is 61.00 km, a ~3 km / ~5% discrepancy. This is the pipeline's OWNER stating a different figure from GEM's, so it is a genuine, sourced disagreement, not noise - but the gap is small and plausibly explained by route-realignment (the same article describes a full GPS re-route survey in 2013 replacing earlier 2004/2009 alignments after benchmark markers were lost/damaged, i.e. the as-built length has itself changed over time) or by rounding/measurement-point differences (pipe centerline vs right-of-way vs field-gate-to-city-gate). Not treating this as a hard 'concern' verdict given the small magnitude and plausible explanation, but recording it as an open spec caveat per the sweep's rule against silently passing disagreements.

validity.recommendation: Leave Capacity as-is (25 MMcf/d) - plausible as nameplate/design capacity - but do not treat it as independently pinned to a verified source; UNRESOLVED for a hard ref.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=25.00 MMcf/d. Open-web (non-verifier-passing) sources describe the Zarghun South field's surface processing facilities as having a design/nameplate capacity of 25 MMSCFD upon 2014 commissioning, which would match GEM cleanly - but I could not get a url_verifier-passing citation for that specific 25 MMSCFD figure (Rigzone's live URL redirect-loops for the verifier; MariEnergies' field-details page and a ResearchGate mirror both 403 the verifier; a GloveNewswire press release timed out). The one primary-source figure I COULD independently verify (via a Wayback Machine snapshot of the Rigzone-hosted Jura Energy Corp press release dated 2014-11-14, which passes url_verifier for 'Zarghun'+'25') actually gives a different number for a different thing: at the moment of full commissioning in Nov 2014, the field was producing 'approximately 17 million cubic feet per day' of sales gas to SSGC (up from ~4 MMcf/d under an interim arrangement) - i.e. actual initial throughput (~17 MMcf/d), not design capacity (~25 MMSCFD per secondary sources). These are not necessarily contradictory (a facility's design capacity is routinely above its initial ramp-up flow), so I am not flagging this as a hard concern, but GEM's 25 MMcf/d has NOT been independently pinned down to a verifier-passing primary source in this pass - recording as an open spec caveat rather than forcing a ref onto it.

summary: P4022 (Zarghun-Quetta Gas Pipeline) is real, correctly classified as an SSGC transmission line, and correctly attributed - confirmed via three independent non-GEM sources (SSGC's own site, a peer-reviewed academic case study, and 2024 Balochistan Post coverage) plus an independently-verified 2014 Jura/Mari Petroleum commissioning press release that corroborates StartYear=2014; no duplicate or classification issue found against the 63-row roster. Two open spec caveats left UNRESOLVED rather than forced: Length (GEM 61 km vs SSGC's own ~64 km, ~5% gap) and Capacity (GEM 25 MMcf/d matches secondary reports of design capacity, but the only verifier-passing primary source instead documents ~17 MMcf/d actual initial throughput).
